01 / Delivery strategy

Build the smallest coherent engineering organization

The architecture is selected; the plan is to integrate and qualify it, not rebuild upstream software. The first milestone proves the containment boundary; the second delivers the first Owner-to-contained-attempt journey. Each later increment adds a verifiable capability without turning the Integration Service into a new workflow engine.

Adopt

Native upstream products

assistant-ui, Agent Canvas, OpenHands, OpenSpec, Backlog.md, Gitea, Task and SQLite retain their native responsibilities.

Own narrowly

Cross-system contracts

Source references, bounded dispatch, operational receipts, owner projections, control/effect enforcement, search authority.

Verify

Actual outcomes

Correct goal, isolated attempt, review independence, protected merge, observed delivery and complete evidence.

The MVP cut line: I0–I2 yields a functioning Owner-to-reviewed-PR workflow. I3 adds authorized consequential delivery. I4 makes prior decisions semantically searchable. I5 makes the full product installable and maintainable across supported platforms. I0–I2 is a development milestone, not permission to deploy unattended effects.

Assumed delivery capacity

One primary autonomous build lane, independent reviewer/security verification, Owner for consequential scope and authority decisions. Parallelize independent work only after the interface and trust contracts are established.

All executable tasks are Small (S); sizes indicate limited scope, not calendar duration. Forecast calendar duration from observed throughput after I1.

Working rules

No long-running gate for routine, reversible Work. Use actual source code and API contracts to resolve compatibility. Record failed tests and limitations. Avoid duplicating Work, conversation streams, Git, a vector store, or a policy engine.

02 / Roadmap and dependencies

Six acceptance milestones

The order is dependency-driven, not a claim that all work within an increment must run serially. Each gate describes a concrete system demonstration.

I0Trustworthy substrateA pinned, reproducible stack can launch a contained, low-privilege OpenHands conversation.I1Intent → contained attemptOwner conversation → accepted goal → ready task → native contained session → source-backed status card.I2Full engineering SDLCAutonomous implementation, early quality checks, independent adversarial review, enforced CI and a protected PR.I3Governed consequencesVersioned controls, protected Owner-only operation merge, independent execution, verified external state and safe recovery.I4Recall + explainHybrid search and source-verified conversation memory; cross-system lineage and evidence-based Owner answers.I5Install, update, restoreInstallable tested composition on Windows, macOS and Linux with backups, updates, license inventory and acceptance proof.
0
Establish the trusted foundation
I0 · Platform + Security · 40 Small tasks

A pinned, reproducible stack can launch a contained, low-privilege OpenHands conversation.

Exit evidence: Demonstrate a session running in its selected execution environment with denied access to Owner secrets, host-management sockets, unauthorized worktrees and prohibited network endpoints.

1
Ship the first Owner-to-agent path
I1 · Experience + Planning + Integration · 37 Small tasks

Owner conversation → accepted goal → ready task → native contained session → source-backed status card.

Exit evidence: An Owner request results in one correctly attributed OpenSpec artifact, Backlog task, OpenHands session and inspectable outcome; reconnect does not duplicate execution.

2
Deliver a reviewed pull request
I2 · Engineering + Quality · 26 Small tasks

Autonomous implementation, early quality checks, independent adversarial review, enforced CI and a protected PR.

Exit evidence: A seeded regression is caught; a failed check blocks merge; a corrected exact revision reaches a reviewed PR with retrievable evidence.

3
Authorize and verify real delivery
I3 · Governance + Security + Delivery · 23 Small tasks

Versioned controls, protected Owner-only operation merge, independent execution, verified external state and safe recovery.

Exit evidence: Agent credentials cannot approve or execute a protected effect; stale approval and replay fail closed; observed result reconciles against authorized manifest.

4
Add organizational memory and observability
I4 · Knowledge + Experience · 14 Small tasks

Hybrid search and source-verified conversation memory; cross-system lineage and evidence-based Owner answers.

Exit evidence: “Why did we choose this?” resolves source messages, accepted design and supersession; unknown/stale and unauthorized records are not presented as authoritative.

5
Qualify the umbrella release
I5 · Release + Platform · 27 Small tasks

Installable tested composition on Windows, macOS and Linux with backups, updates, license inventory and acceptance proof.

Exit evidence: A fresh installation, reviewed change, interrupted upgrade and restored durable state pass the defined platform and security acceptance contracts.

F-07.1Define and implement the managed data root and configuration contractStep 1/2 of F-07 · Foundation & platforms · I0 · S complexity · 1 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

F-07 — Externalize installation, configuration and data ownership. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Define and implement the managed data root and configuration contract: an OS-appropriate external default root (Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\AIEH\, Linux per XDG), resolved through an established cross-platform path library or the platform conventions, with three top-level lifecycle categories beneath it, persistent/ (durable workspaces, databases, credentials, authorization records, configuration and operational evidence), ephemeral/ (disposable scratch, temporary execution artifacts, caches and regenerable intermediate files) and assets/ (downloaded, reusable, verified artifacts such as pinned model weights, VM base images, installation packages and third-party distributions, each retaining version, provenance, integrity metadata and enough information to reacquire it, deleted only deliberately and reclaimable only when no required consumer depends on it and verified reacquisition is possible), with base images kept distinct from mutable VM disks and overlays, which belong in persistent/ or ephemeral/ by lifecycle; the optional AIEH_DATA_ROOT override, absolute or relative, a relative override resolving against the repository root, never the cwd; a data root inside or containing the source checkout is refused; a tracked example_config.yml and an optional, gitignored config.yml for non-secret settings and per-directory overrides, a relative directory override resolving against the effective root; deterministic precedence of a per-directory override, then AIEH_DATA_ROOT, then the OS default; one shared resolver with thin adapters across language and process boundaries; an evaluation of dotenv as optional convenience only; no secrets in tracked or source-accessible configuration.

Required output

Contract decision, example_config.yml, the shared resolver and its adapters, and tests of the resolution acceptance criteria.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

A fresh checkout works without config.yml or .env; default state lives outside the checkout; the root has three top-level lifecycle categories, persistent/ (durable workspaces, databases, credentials, authorization records, configuration and operational evidence), ephemeral/ (disposable scratch, temporary execution artifacts, caches and regenerable intermediate files) and assets/ (downloaded, reusable, verified artifacts such as pinned model weights, VM base images, installation packages and third-party distributions, each retaining version, provenance, integrity metadata and enough information to reacquire it, deleted only deliberately and reclaimable only when no required consumer depends on it and verified reacquisition is possible), with base images kept distinct from mutable VM disks and overlays, which belong in persistent/ or ephemeral/ by lifecycle; the platform defaults follow convention; AIEH_DATA_ROOT relocates the whole root; relative root overrides resolve against the checkout and relative directory overrides against the effective root; absolute overrides work; a data root inside or containing the source checkout is refused; resolution is cwd-independent; invalid configuration fails with actionable errors; no drive-root directories are created.

F-07.2Adopt the contract across components and plan data migrationStep 2/2 of F-07 · Foundation & platforms · I0 · S complexity · 1 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

F-07 — Externalize installation, configuration and data ownership. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Inventory filesystem behaviour across installation scripts, Python and PowerShell tooling, guest provisioning, container configuration, stores, logs, caches, temp files, fixtures and build artifacts; move every component's path choices onto the shared resolver; classify existing project-created data (regenerable, installed binaries, service databases, durable workspaces, credentials and authorization state, operational evidence, unknown or user-owned) and give a reversible migration and cleanup strategy, with no automatic moves or deletion and no breakage of active installations; plan the migration of the existing guest-state root by first inventorying and classifying its contents into persistent/, ephemeral/ and assets/, not by moving the whole tree, as a copy, then integrity verification, then a reference switch, then a separately authorized cleanup, preserving the existing authorization and custody checks and not interrupting active guest workflows; perform no migration in this leaf; record the dogfooding trust boundary, so that the managed root is never exposed to source-editing agents through workspace mounts, tool permissions or inherited credentials. Decide and implement a class-E category for authorization records (the approved-input manifest), the effects category, the effects store's location policy and the relocation-exposure report (decision 0010), and where exported exchange evidence survives a fresh-mode guest destroy.

Required output

Filesystem inventory, component adoption of the shared resolver, the migration plan and the trust-boundary update.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

Components consume resolved paths; persistent state survives restarts and upgrades; nothing is implicitly deleted; the contents of the existing guest-state root are inventoried and classified into persistent/, ephemeral/ and assets/, and its migration plan is copy, integrity verification, reference switch and separately authorized cleanup, preserving authorization and custody checks, with no active guest workflow interrupted and no migration performed; relocating the checkout does not break the installed system; a source-editing agent's grant gives no access to installed secrets or protected operational state; the existing confinement invariants still hold. The approved-input manifest resolves to the class-E category for authorization records; the effects store resolves to the effects category under the decided location policy and reports relocation exposure (decision 0010); exported exchange evidence of a destroyed fresh-mode guest survives the destroy in its decided location.

Non-executable parent

F-06 — Host the local Git service. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Pin the Windows asset of the pinned Gitea 28.3.0 release by hash, to the existing three-source provenance standard; keep the verified binary as an asset at the shared resolver's assets location (<data-root>/assets/...) and run Gitea with its persistent state at the shared resolver's location (default <data-root>/persistent/gitea/), bound only to 127.0.0.1, under the current Windows user without administrator rights, with no WSL and no VM; keep credentials and tokens outside the source checkout and tracked artifacts; preserve the distinction between the site-administrator credential and the separate non-administrator Owner identity, and follow the existing authorization requirements before creating credentials; tie Gitea's lifetime to the managed environment.

Required output

Gitea lifecycle commands, the pinned Windows asset digest, and a disposable-instance qualification record.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

The binary hash equals the pin; Gitea listens only on 127.0.0.1, runs without elevation, uses only resolver-provided paths outside the checkout, refuses anonymous registration, keeps no credential in the checkout, and stops when the managed environment shuts down.

Non-executable parent

F-06 — Host the local Git service. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Extract the host-service lifecycle contract and the Windows adapter from the existing Gitea host tooling with no behaviour change, and add the restart and inspect verbs: integrations/platform/ holds platform_contract.py and platform_windows.py (platform_linux.py and platform_darwin.py follow in F-06.4 and F-06.5), and gitea_host.py composes the platform adapter and the credential provider; the contract's verbs are install, up, down, restart, status, inspect and verify, credential provision, rotate and retire, and upgrade, recover and uninstall; its records are aieh-platform/1 (system, machine, asset_key, supervision, credentials), aieh-asset/1, aieh-gitea-host/1 (with an optional platform.asset_key), aieh-service-run/1 (generalising aieh-gitea-run/1, which readers still accept), aieh-readiness/1 (platform-neutral check names, each record carrying its platform) and aieh-service-transition/1; refusals keep the existing codes and add PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED, PLATFORM_MISMATCH, SUPERVISION_UNAVAILABLE, NO_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER, CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_LOCKED, VERSION_MISMATCH, DOWNGRADE_REFUSED, TRANSITION_PENDING and UNINSTALL_RUNNING, each with a remedy; Windows supervision stays a Job Object with kill-on-close and inspection the TCP table and the process token, without psutil; give the documentation's verified table per-OS columns with rows per verb and the provider, and record the Windows result in its own evidence file.

Required output

integrations/platform/ (the lifecycle contract and the Windows adapter), gitea_host.py composed over it, the generalised records and refusal codes, and the Windows evidence record.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

On Windows: gitea:verify gives identical results on the live instance before and after the extraction; all existing tests and the live test pass; credential invariant I7 holds (a no-exposure scan follows every act); every readiness record carries its platform.

F-06.3Credential provider adoption (keyring for POSIX; Windows provider kept; fail closed)Step 3/6 of F-06 · Foundation & platforms · I0 · S complexity · 2 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

F-06 — Host the local Git service. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Add integrations/credentials/credential_provider.py: the CredentialProvider interface; the existing standard-library ctypes Windows provider, moved, with keyring kept off Windows; a KeyringProvider for POSIX that instantiates keyring's macOS.Keyring() or SecretService.Keyring() explicitly and checks its .priority, never get_keyring(), a keyringrc, PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND, the keyring CLI or keyrings.alt; a fail-closed factory in which the harness chooses the backend; and doctor. Copy the keyring 25.7.0 (MIT) pins and their dependencies, already hash-locked in the F-01.2 locks, into tools-requirements.txt with sys_platform markers; the POSIX lifecycle runs under the tools venv. Add a provider contract suite (a fake, the Windows provider, and keyring with an in-process backend) and a throwaway-name cross-read test. Credential invariants I1-I8 hold for every act: (1) never printed, logged, on a command line or in an environment variable; (2) one named entry per credential; (3) stored before the change; (4) every act can be rerun and resumes; (5) fail closed; (6) the backend is chosen by the harness; (7) a no-exposure scan follows every act; (8) reports carry fingerprints only.

Required output

integrations/credentials/credential_provider.py with doctor and the provider contract suite, and the keyring pins in the tools lock.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

On Windows: tools:install installs keyring wheels-only from the hash-locked tools lock; the live credential entries are untouched and gitea:authz passes; the provider contract suite and the throwaway-name cross-read test pass; with no qualified provider the factory refuses with NO_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER. Every rotate or retire act writes an integration-store receipt (fingerprints only) and reads it back; an act without a receipt read back is a failure. Decision 0011 is committed to decisions/.

F-06.4Linux adapter and verification on a real Linux hostStep 4/6 of F-06 · Foundation & platforms · I0 · S complexity · 1 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

F-06 — Host the local Git service. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Implement platform_linux.py under the host-service lifecycle contract and verify it on the existing disposable Debian test guest (QEMU), used as a headless Linux host under its current isolation rules (decision 0003): pin the Linux asset of the pinned Gitea 28.3.0 release for the guest's architecture by hash, to the three-source provenance standard, and bring it to the guest only through the existing exchange or provisioning channel (decision 0006), since the guest has no network; supervise Gitea as a systemd-run --user transient service with KillMode=control-group, using the PR_SET_PDEATHSIG process-group fallback only where configuration explicitly enables it; inspect it through /proc/net/tcp, the process's file descriptors and /proc/<pid>/status; bind it only to 127.0.0.1; for headless credential custody qualify systemd-creds --user (systemd 256 or later) as a credential provider, and fail closed until it qualifies; use keyring's explicit Secret Service backend where a Secret Service is present; add the Linux column to the verified table and record the result in its own Linux evidence file. Any expansion of the guest's host access, network or privileges needs separate Owner authorization.

Required output

platform_linux.py, the qualified headless credential provider, the pinned Linux asset digest and the Linux evidence record.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

On Linux (the Debian test guest): the binary hash equals the pin; readiness passes with platform linux and Gitea listens only on 127.0.0.1; killing the transient unit and logging out each end Gitea; the credential round trip passes through systemd-creds --user (systemd 256 or later) for headless custody, and through the Secret Service backend where a Secret Service is present; without a qualified provider the lifecycle refuses with NO_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER; the refusal paths return their stable codes and remedies; credential invariants I1-I8 hold; the result is recorded in its own Linux evidence record. One test:profile --counters-only run on Linux records the POSIX launch events (within F-06.4's own guest authorization, when granted).

F-06.6Upgrade, recovery and uninstall semantics of the host serviceStep 6/6 of F-06 · Foundation & platforms · I0 · S complexity · 2 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

F-06 — Host the local Git service. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Implement upgrade, recovery and uninstall under the host-service lifecycle contract: keep the desired, staged and running versions distinct; write a write-ahead aieh-service-transition/1 record before each transition; upgrade --to backs up gitea.db with the SQLite backup API and app.ini, and rolls back automatically before verification and only on an Owner decision after it; recover reconciles the actual state first; uninstall deletes nothing under persistent/ and no asset; refuse with VERSION_MISMATCH, DOWNGRADE_REFUSED, TRANSITION_PENDING or UNINSTALL_RUNNING, each with a remedy; rehearse on a disposable Windows instance.

Required output

The upgrade, recover and uninstall verbs, the aieh-service-transition/1 record and the disposable-instance rehearsal record.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

On Windows (a disposable instance): an upgrade, an automatic rollback of a failure before verification, an interrupted transition resumed by recover, and an uninstall each leave the state the contract specifies, reconciled from the write-ahead record; gitea.db and app.ini are backed up before each upgrade; uninstall leaves persistent/ and every asset in place; a downgrade, a transition while one is pending and an uninstall while Gitea runs are refused with their codes. Gitea survives a host reboot or sign-out, or stops as the lifecycle contract says, and the lifecycle state is reported correctly afterwards; Gitea's outbound proxy and egress settings are inspected and recorded.

S-03 — Broker model access. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Within decision 0015 as amended (amendment 1), implement the inference broker and the model-access plane (family-bound per-attempt tokens, per-family untranslated pass-through, the guest inference endpoint and its forward, the guest composition, egress and audit), built and tested offline with synthetic credentials and a fake upstream per declared API family; then qualify the plane's denial paths and containment in one disposable guest, without a model.

Required output

The inference broker, its configuration and offline fixture suite (synthetic credentials, a fake upstream per declared API family), and the plane's denial-path and containment qualification record.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

Within decision 0015 as amended, the broker is built and tested offline with synthetic credentials and a fake upstream per declared API family. In one disposable guest, a probe from inside a conversation container shows 401 without a token, forwarding to a fake upstream with a valid family-bound token, immediate refusal after revocation, fail-closed loss of the forward, and every other target refused. Agents cannot read the provider credential: shown with a synthetic key served by the qualification-only launcher, searched for at the secret's exposure boundaries (the guest's files, process environments and records, the jobs, the instance directory and the reports) in its raw form and its common encodings by a checker that holds it in memory only and reports counts, with a positive control showing the search finds a planted copy; a fingerprint search alone is not described as proof that the raw credential is absent, and the real key's containment is S-03.3's; egress beyond the broker is denied. With the plane in place, the full containment catalogue is re-run and every deviation's compensating cases still PASS. The denial and containment evidence is independent of the broker's own report. The probe creates a child conversation from inside the conversation container through the inner server's children route with the conversation's own key (the route and key the start_child_conversation tool uses, S-01.3.1). If a child is created, it is observed in the parent's container under the same limits, with no new container, no new listener and no conversation on the outer server. If the inner server refuses the creation without model settings, the refusal is recorded as a demonstrated fail-closed outcome, not as proof that a child ran or was contained; successful child containment then stays unverified, as a traceable obligation of S-03.3 (the ACP provider's delegation) and of the first leaf that enables the native start_child_conversation tool (A-01.2's gate). No model call is made.

P-04.2Build the Owner authorization recorderStep 2/3 of P-04 · Intent & planning · I1 · S complexity · 2 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

P-04 — Record Owner decisions. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Build the deterministic, non-model Owner authorization recorder and exercise it on the S-01.2.2 fixture. It is the sole custodian of cred-gitea-owner-account, authenticates as aieh-owner with basic auth held in memory per call, never mints a token, never uses sudo, force_merge or auto-merge, makes merge commits only, has no agent-callable or MCP surface, and runs only in the main session on an Owner decision. prepare <repo> <pr> writes a challenge (operation, PR, exact head, manifest digest, nonce and expiry) to the recorder's own state; record --challenge --statement refuses, each with a stable code, unless authenticity (its own unexpired, unconsumed nonce; an Owner-attributed statement naming the operation id; an admitted channel), binding (an open PR against the protected branch; head and manifest blob digest equal to the challenged ones; the manifest is the single file operations/<id>.json; a new operation id; an author other than aieh-owner), freshness (both expiries unpassed; the PR mergeable), policy (the protection and repository rules exactly as expected), identity (aieh-owner non-admin with zero tokens) and single use all hold. It writes the Owner decision record in the shared shape (kind authorize-operation) and a write-ahead receipt of a new append-only kind to the integration store, never the effects store; merges with Do: merge and head_commit_id, the message carrying the trailers AIEH-Decision-Id, AIEH-Decision-Channel, AIEH-Approved-Head, AIEH-Manifest-Digest, AIEH-Statement-Ref and AIEH-Recorder; reads back the ref, the parent, the digest and merged_by; and resolves a lost answer as unknown by reading the ref, never by merging again. The bootstrap channel is the Owner's verbatim reply in the main-session conversation after the challenge is shown, transcribed by the Overseer and logged with the decision id; it proves a declared decision bound to an exact revision, not an authenticated Owner. merged_by aieh-owner is shown as merged under Owner authority by the recorder on decision <id>, never as merged by the Owner. Update security/inventory.json (an authorization-recorder principal as custodian of cred-gitea-owner-account; op-protected-merge keeps principal owner with the recorder as delegated performer; fd-owner-authorization-record narrowed) and policy/role-tokens.json (the owner row's realization and issuance text, and a custodian row); record decision 0012 and a blueprint reconciliation item for #experience step 16 and the #decisions phrase 'no automation merge'.

Required output

The Owner authorization recorder, its Owner decision records and integration-store receipt kind, its fixtures and negative suite, and decision 0012.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

A recorded decision gives exactly one merge, bound to the approved head and manifest digest, with an integration-store receipt and the trailers; each of these is refused with its stable code: a stale head (Gitea's 409), an altered digest, a replayed or expired decision, a missing or non-Owner statement, a missing challenge, protection drift, and a token on aieh-owner; no token is minted, and every bot token is refused both for the recorder's inputs and for the merge. Decision 0012 is committed to decisions/. An inspection shows that the Owner credential exists only in its OS credential-provider entry: no file copy, and absent from every agent and job environment. The same-account limit is recorded (decision 0010).

Non-executable parent

E-01.4 — Reconcile lost create responses and interrupted requests. Higher-level group: E-01. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

From the locked openhands-agent-server 1.60.1 source and the E-01.2.2(c) journals (finding F-15; E-01.2.2(b) F-5), establish the root cause of the intermittent start failure (the main process exits 1 about 1.5 s after start; 2 of 272 restarts; inference: litellm's cost-map retry thread imports a partly initialised module while the guest has no network). Adopt an upstream configuration control that removes the trigger, declared in the profile and requalified per QUALIFICATION.md, or record why none exists. Declare the start path's failure handling (systemd restart and the readiness ceiling) so that a retried or slow start is reported as such, never as a clean start. File the upstream report and record its reference; the report does not discharge this leaf.

Required output

The root-cause record, the profile declaration of the control or of the bounded limit, the start-failure handling declaration, the restart-series evidence and the upstream report reference.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

Decision rule fixed before observation. With a control: 0 main-process exits during start in at least 500 consecutive Agent Server restarts on a fresh disposable guest at the fixed commit (at the observed 2 in 272 an unchanged server passes with probability about 2.5%), and the requalification the profile rules require passes. Without a control: over 500 restarts every failed start is retried and reaches readiness within the declared ceiling, the maximum and the distribution of start times are recorded, and the limit is recorded in security/inventory.json or the profile with its reconsider condition (an upstream fix in a pinned release, re-observed by R-01.2). Either way, the readiness wait reports a retried or slow start distinctly, and the upstream report reference is recorded.

Verify native runtime, effective workspace/mounts, and source reference before marking the attempt launched. Surface mismatch/unknown to Owner projection. Inspect each attempt's container independently, and refuse an ordinal that would overlap an executing attempt.

Required output

Dispatch acceptance evidence and fail-closed result mapping.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

No unauthorized workspace path or local-runtime fallback is reported as an accepted attempt; original parent proof remains satisfied. Per attempt, an independent docker inspect shows caps, image ID and mounts equal to the admitted ones, and NetworkMode and ExtraHosts equal exactly to the recorded limit values of fd-container-network-deviations; any other value marks the attempt not launched. Execution non-overlap (review finding 1): no ordinal N+1 is reserved or dispatched for a Work, design revision and stage while ordinal N's conversation is executing as the Agent Server reports it, and an unknown execution state also refuses; acceptance tests prove both refusals. The lineage attempt resolver resolves the dispatched attempt.

G-04.2.1Provision executor principal and isolated operation environmentStep 1/2 of G-04.2 · Delivery & authorization · I3 · S complexity · 1 prerequisitesP0›
Non-executable parent

G-04.2 — Provision isolated executor identity and storage. Higher-level group: G-04. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Provision the executor principal, an allowlisted operation interface and protected credential-delivery configuration, with the executor's code and configuration managed under the managed data root (persistent/installs/ or another managed location, with defaults); before any privileged operation the executor validates its identity, configuration, authorization and integrity, and fails closed when any check fails. Per decision 0010, no restricted executor account, privileged installation location, elevated setup or OS-isolated file permissions are introduced solely against same-account attacks; a same-account modification or relocation of the installation is detected where the integrity checks can detect it, and is not by itself grounds for refusing to operate.

Required output

Executor runtime profile and principal permissions matrix.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

Agent and CI principals cannot invoke or impersonate executor.

Non-executable parent

R-01 — Compose a releasable pinned umbrella. Run this small leaf only, not its parent.

Bounded agent work

Generate manifest checks and installed/running version probes; require qualification when component lock changes. On a lock change of an execution component, re-run the containment catalogue and inspect before the change is accepted.

Required output

Composition reconcile script and release-manifest acceptance fixture.

Acceptance evidence — exit gate

Observed revisions match declared release or fail visibly; original R-01 proof satisfied. Any change to the Agent Server binary, conversation image, Moby, guest image, kernel, apt snapshot or QEMU pin re-runs the S-02.1 containment catalogue (security/containment-cases.json) and inspect; every deviation case and its compensating cases PASS, or the lock change is refused. The run re-checks whether upstream now offers a control for host-gateway or the container network; if one exists, a recorded decision adopts it or states why not. It re-observes the F-04.2 upstream behaviours (VSCode server, tool preload, resolver, cost-map fetch, leftover files) and the image's engine-client and setuid content. A QEMU pin change re-qualifies XSAVE (-cpu).

03A / Execution prompts

Overseer-directed agent workflow

Each of the 167 Small leaves has its own standalone prompt for the Overseer. The Overseer delegates actual changes to Builder, consults Architect only for consequential design uncertainty, and retains responsibility for independent acceptance and dependency gating.

OverseerAdmit, prioritize and coordinate
→
Architect (conditional)Resolve real design or security ambiguity
→
BuilderProduce the artifact and measured checks
→
OverseerVerify, record evidence, unlock dependencies
Claude Code session guidance: Start a new Overseer session with /clear, then paste the operating prompt below. For a targeted task, continue in that same Overseer session and paste the corresponding task prompt; use /clear only when restarting and resend the operating prompt. The user does not have to relay instructions separately to Architect or Builder.

When to involve Architect

Unsettled API/interface contracts, trust and authorization boundaries, source authority, database/schema evolution, component changes, consequential tradeoffs or conflicting accepted requirements. Demand an actionable scoped decision and evidence.

When to go straight to Builder

Well-specified integration, configuration, targeted research artifacts, tests, docs, and bounded improvements whose design is already accepted. Builder writes and verifies; Overseer checks independent evidence and original parent gates.

Master operating prompt

Paste once to launch coordinated execution of the plan. Individual prompt blocks are available inside each task card below and in the downloadable prompt pack.

Important: these prompts describe planned tasks and required evidence. They do not authorize privileged operations, establish that dependencies have passed, or assert any task is complete.

One Small step per agent attempt

The previous 59 Medium tasks and 12 original Large outcomes remain non-executable acceptance groups. Only Small leaves in JSON work_packages may be dispatched. Every leaf must produce an observable artifact and reproducible evidence before the next dependency becomes eligible.

Agent operation contract

Admission

Select only a leaf whose dependencies have passed. Resolve its approved architecture revision, agent/Skill digest, available tools and resource limits. Original Large and Medium IDs are aliases for acceptance groups and must never be sent as jobs.

Completion

Produce the listed artifact and independently check its precise exit criterion. Persist exact source revisions, run/test IDs and result as pass/fail/unknown. Before releasing downstream Work, validate any inherited Medium and Large acceptance gates explicitly.

Retained Large outcome contracts

The 12 original Large packages remain traceable with their original acceptance. Their earlier intermediate Medium children are also preserved in decomposition.medium_parent_outcomes, but only the new Small steps are executable.

Original outcomeExecutable descendantsOriginal acceptance
F-03 — Define and provision a managed execution VMFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small stepsGuest provision and teardown do not mount Owner secrets or uncontrolled host folders.
S-01 — Separate identities, credentials and network planesFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small stepsAn agent cannot invoke privileged conversation creation or access Owner/admin tokens even if it controls its own workspace.
E-01 — Reserve and dispatch a contained Work attemptFirst leaf · Last leaf · 11 small stepsRepeated create/lost response rejoins the same conversation; no unauthorized workspace path or local-runtime fallback.
E-03 — Run independent implementation and review contextsFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small stepsReviewer reports a seeded real defect; review can block acceptance; agent profiles and model adapters are versioned.
Q-02 — Isolate untrusted CI runnersFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small stepsUntrusted PR tests cannot read protected secrets or privileged host paths.
E-04 — Close review findings through bounded reworkFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small stepsA rejected change does not become accepted Work; successful rework yields a new reviewed and validated SHA.
G-04 — Build an independent bounded effect executorFirst leaf · Last leaf · 9 small stepsForged webhook, stale merge and replay cannot cause unauthorized or duplicate effects; unknown outcome stops safely.
G-06 — Prove controls and recovery at consequential boundariesFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small stepsFailures block only relevant effects; authorized exceptions remain visible and expire rather than changing a failing control to passed.
K-03 — Resolve current authority and supersession at retrieval timeFirst leaf · Last leaf · 6 small steps“What did we decide?” differentiates tentative discussion from accepted and superseded decisions; denied records never leak.
R-02 — Implement backup, activation and safe rollbackFirst leaf · Last leaf · 8 small stepsInterrupted activation reconciles actual version; durable repos, threads, Work and effect receipts survive update/restart.
R-03 — Package and qualify Windows, macOS and LinuxFirst leaf · Last leaf · 8 small stepsSame Owner-to-reviewed-change scenario passes on each supported OS under qualified resource/network profile.
R-05 — Run product acceptance and publish the initial releaseFirst leaf · Last leaf · 7 small stepsAll milestone gates and platform/security tests pass; if any required result is unknown, release status cannot be green.
Scheduling: Dependencies encode eligibility, not priority or dates. Parallel execution is permitted only when independent source/credential and SQLite write boundaries allow it. If an artifact, gate or source is unknown, stop that chain and retain the existing evidence.
04 / Integration sequencing

The dependency spine that governs delivery

These are the handoffs where independent upstream products must agree about identity, authority, or observed state. Prioritize these contracts over broad component configuration or optional enhancements.

First independently contained attempt

Foundation

VM profile → native runtime → trusted API boundary → negative-access probe.

Planning

OpenSpec objective → ready Backlog task → source references.

Dispatch

SQLite reservation → OpenHands create/reconcile → Owner status projection.

First authorized verified effect

Quality

isolated CI → required checks → review/rework.

Repository

reviewed code PR → Owner-only manifest merge.

Effect

isolated executor → observed delivery verdict → negative assurance.

Architecture constraint: Direct contained dispatch is the normal Work path. OpenHands Automation supplies optional scheduled/event triggers through the same admission and receipt contract. Avoid implementing a second general-purpose scheduler, workflow language or container orchestrator.
05 / SDLC and acceptance

Quality is built in early; promotion is enforced independently

Agent reasoning and local checks are feedback. Security, authorization and promotion depend on enforcing systems that agents cannot alter.

Before implementationNormalize the goal, map acceptance, identify design risks and applicable controls. Reject untrusted instructions as authority.
During implementationSmall diffs, formatting/linting, focused tests, type checks, threat-guided verification and changed-line coverage.
Independent CI and reviewSeparate reviewer; isolated runner; protected required checks against the exact commit; security and supply-chain scans.
After deliverySeparate authorization if consequential; verify real target state; evidence, exceptions, failure and residual risk remain linked to original intent.
BoundaryEnforcerEvidence requiredFailure behavior
Agent launchManaged VM + restricted brokerResolved profile, effective mounts/network, execution UUID and negative-access probeDo not launch or stop contained attempt
Code qualityAgent sandbox + independent Gitea CIFormatter/linter/tests/coverage tool results for exact SHAReturn to same Work for rework
Adversarial reviewDistinct review session/providerSource-linked findings, addressed regressions, reviewed SHAKeep task unaccepted, rework on new revision
Control enforcementProtected policy + actual security/CI/executor boundaryControl ID/version, subject/revision, observation and freshnessFailed/unknown/stale cannot silently pass
Consequence authorizationOwner-only Gitea merge + isolated effect executorExact merged manifest digest, authorized identity, effect receipt and observed targetReject replay/stale/forged requests
Outcome acceptanceSource-backed acceptance resolverEach criterion satisfied, failed, unknown or explicitly exceptedNever claim complete from agent/CI/merge success alone
Definition of Done: The source-backed objective is met; mandatory checks and independent review pass on the delivered revision; controls are satisfied or authorized exceptions are recorded; all consequential operations are permitted and verified; the Owner can follow the lineage from intent to effect.

Risk / issueMitigation in planOwner-visible trigger

Untrusted CI steals host or promotion credentialsDistinct runners and restricted tokens (Q-02), deny CI promotion credentialsCI negative-access test fails

Explicitly deferred from the initial implementation

Independent workflow engine / DBOS

Existing native dispatch + receipts cover first integration; reconsider only on demonstrated recovery failure.

Universal event renderer / AG-UI bridge

Agent Canvas already renders native OpenHands events; do not double stream.

Full ontology/graph DB / separate vector server

Hybrid SQLite retrieval and source authority resolver meet initial need.

OpenTofu / Kubernetes / bespoke microVM manager

Native Incus/Lima configuration is sufficient for local-first profiles.

Custom GRC platform

Protected control catalog and native CI evidence suffice; OSCAL interoperability optional.

Automated model self-improvement platform

Evaluate only once observable engineering benchmarks justify complexity.

Podman as default runtime

Moby remains native compatibility baseline; Podman is an alternative after interface qualification.

07 / Ownership, governance and first actions

How implementation work should be delegated

Roles are responsibilities, not mandatory headcount. Most work can be executed by coding agents, with independent review/security checks and narrowly scoped Owner decisions.

Decision or activityAccountable roleEvidence or handoff
Set original objective, material constraints and consequence toleranceOwnerOriginal conversation → accepted OpenSpec goal
Translate intent, architecture and dependencies into executable WorkPlanning agentOpenSpec design revision + Backlog task graph
Build integrations and package providersEngineering agentCommit + CI evidence + run/Skill identity
Challenge implementation and securityIndependent reviewer / security roleAdversarial findings and control observations
Accept consequential design tradeoffs or authorize external effectOwner / Gitea protected authoritySource-linked decision or protected operation merge
Apply and verify privileged operationsIsolated executorOperation receipt and observed state
Explain progress and final verdictRead-only Integration Service projectionLinked source and evidence, not a parallel Work status

First three concrete actions (Small leaf-task IDs)

  1. F-01: pin an upstream OpenHands/Canvas compatibility set and distribution dependencies.
  2. F-02: establish the umbrella repository and repeatable setup/test entrypoints.
  3. F-03 + F-05: establish host execution profile and trusted SQLite receipts in parallel where possible.

When to revisit the plan

Replan if an upstream supported interface is absent at the pinned revision; a mandatory security control cannot be enforced; data durability/restore fails; a provider changes compatibility or terms; or the cost of a custom adapter exceeds adopting a better upstream alternative.

Don't replan merely because tests discover ordinary implementation defects—return those to the relevant Work item.
